title: introduce-token-stage-cohorting-and-route-matrix-alerting
author: Maya Chen
commits: feat(observability): add token_stage_cohort service and in-memory index
feat(alerts): route-matrix alert generator and policy bindings
ui(dashboards): token-stage cohort dashboard and cohort drift panel
test: add integration tests for cohorting and alert routing
description: Context: long-tail token cost and multi-stage latency spikes frequently surface only when a request traverses several model-serving stages (tokenization, encoder, decode, fallback). Existing alerts were per-route and per-quantile but lacked a compact way to group requests by 'stage footprint' and automatically route alerting weight to the stage(s) most likely responsible. Motivation: reduce alert noise and accelerate RCA by grouping invocations into stage-aware cohorts and deriving a route x stage alert matrix that attributes SLO violations to the most likely pipeline stage. What this PR does: 1) Adds a lightweight token_stage_cohort service that computes a deterministic cohort key per invocation based on stage-level metrics (token counts per stage, kv-cache hit pattern, decode-batch size) and stores short-lived cohort aggregates. 2) Introduces an alert route-matrix generator that consumes cohort rollups and emits alert bindings which bias escalation to the top-k stages for that route. 3) Adds a new dashboard focused on cohort drift, stage heatmaps, and per-cohort cost/latency breakdown to help oncall quickly validate root cause hypotheses. 4) Wires the generator into the existing alerting pipeline with a safe canary rollout and automatic quiet-window attenuation to avoid regressing noise. Compatibility and rollout: service defaults to read-only mode until flagged by a feature flag; alert generation starts cross-account in a low-sensitivity mode (only P90/P99) and is then ramped after 72h of monitoring. Testing: unit and integration tests added; ran a 48h synthetic replay against production-like traces (see test run in CI). Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Dashboard panels - [x] Docs for oncall and runbook - [x] Feature-flagged rollout Plan for operators: deploy to staging -> enable feature flag -> monitor cohort drift and false-positive rate -> bump sensitivity -> full rollout. Links: Linear ENG-1248 (cohorting design) and PM-432 (dashboard spec).
review_comments: Diego: Can cohort keys be stable across model version rollouts? Added suggestion to include model-version hash in key derivation. Response: we now namespace cohort keys with model-major-version and include fallback mapping in cohort_store.proto.

Priya: Alert noise risk—please limit initial sensitivity and provide quiet-window behavior. Response: implemented quiet-window attenuation and low-sensitivity defaults; documented in docs/observability/token-cohorting.md.

Liam: test coverage looks good but add an e2e replay with partial KV-cache misses. Response: added synthetic KV miss replay in tests/integration/test_cohorting_flow.py and CI run shows stable results.
ci_details: e2e: flaky on first run -> rerun succeeded
release_notes: Add stage-aware token cohorting and a route-stage alert matrix to improve SLO attribution. Feature is behind a flag and rolled out in low-sensitivity mode by default.
notes_for_oncall: When an alert references a cohort key, open the cohort dashboard and inspect stage heatmap and token cost splits. If cohort drift is high (drift_score > 0.2) treat initial attributions as low confidence and follow runbook section 'cohortized-rca'.
risk_and_mitigation: Noise risk mitigated via low-sensitivity default and quiet-window attenuation; breaking changes avoided by read-only default and namespacing cohort keys with model-major-version.
